questions.subject: C
questions.question: In C, what does the declaration int (*(*fp)(int))[5]; represent?

options.A: A function taking int and returning array of 5 pointers
options.B: A pointer to a function taking an int argument and returning a pointer to an array of 5 integers

questions.explanation: Reading right-left rule: fp is a pointer (*) to a function (int) returning a pointer (*) to an array [5] of int.

questions.subject: C
questions.explanation: modify accepts address of pointer &p. *pp = &val updates p in main to point to static variable val (50).

questions.subject: C
questions.question: How do you declare a function pointer named 'func' that points to a function taking two double parameters and returning an int?
questions.explanation: int (*func)(double, double); correctly declares a function pointer. Without parentheses, int *func(...) declares a function returning an int pointer.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: Given int arr[3][4]; what is the data type of the expression 'arr' when decayed in an expression?
questions.explanation: When a 2D array decays, it yields a pointer to its first row element, which has type pointer-to-array-of-4-ints: int (*)[4].

questions.subject: C
questions.question: Assuming a standard 64-bit ABI with 4-byte int alignment and 8-byte double alignment, what is sizeof(struct Data) for struct Data { char c; int i; double d; };?
questions.explanation: char c (1 byte) + 3 padding bytes -> int i (4 bytes at offset 4) -> double d (8 bytes at offset 8). Total size = 16 bytes.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the function of token-pasting operator ## in C preprocessor macro #define CONCAT(a, b) a ## b?

options.B: Merges two tokens a and b into a single syntactical token during preprocessing

questions.explanation: The ## operator pastes tokens together. CONCAT(var, 1) expands to the token var1.

questions.subject: C
questions.topic: Dynamic memory management and memory leaks
questions.question: What constitutes a memory leak when using realloc() like ptr = realloc(ptr, new_size);?

options.B: If realloc fails and returns NULL, assigning back to 'ptr' overwrites the original address, losing the reference to original block
options.D: Memory leaks only occur with calloc

questions.explanation: Overwriting original pointer with NULL on realloc failure causes reference loss to original memory block, leaking it.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the result of evaluating expression i = i++ + 1; in C17?

options.C: Undefined Behavior due to unsequenced side effect and value computation on 'i'

questions.explanation: In C11/C17 standard rules, modifying a scalar object more than once without intermediate sequence points yields Undefined Behavior.

questions.subject: C
questions.topic: Strict aliasing and effective type fundamentals
questions.question: What is the Strict Aliasing Rule in C compiler optimization?

options.A: Pointers of different types cannot point to same memory address unless one is char* or void*
options.B: Compiler assumes pointers of incompatible types do not alias the same memory location, enabling optimization

questions.explanation: Strict aliasing allows compilers to assume pointers to incompatible types do not refer to the same memory object.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the worst-case space complexity of recursive implementation of Depth-First Search (DFS) on a graph with V vertices due to call stack?
questions.explanation: In worst case (path graph), call stack recursion depth reaches O(V) frames.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: In Floyd's Cycle Detection Algorithm (Tortoise and Hare) on a linked list, why are cycle detected when fast pointer moves 2 steps and slow moves 1 step?

options.B: Relative distance between fast and slow pointers decreases by 1 in each loop iteration inside cycle
options.C: Slow pointer stops at cycle entry

questions.explanation: In a cycle, the loop gap shrinks by (2-1)=1 node per iteration, guaranteeing convergence without infinite loop.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What operation does expression x & (x - 1) perform on a non-zero integer x?

options.B: Clears the lowest set bit (rightmost 1-bit) in x

questions.explanation: x & (x - 1) turns off the lowest set bit of x. It is frequently used to check if x is a power of 2 (x & (x - 1) == 0).

questions.subject: C
questions.question: Why should file reading loops check feof() AFTER a read operation (like fread or fgetc) rather than in loop condition while(!feof(fp))?

options.B: feof() returns true only AFTER an attempted read past EOF fails, causing an extra loop iteration if checked first
options.C: feof() works only for text files

questions.explanation: feof() is set only after a read operation attempts to read past EOF. Checking before reading processes the last byte twice.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: In executable memory layout (ELF), where are uninitialized global and static variables stored?
questions.explanation: Uninitialized global/static variables are placed in BSS segment and initialized to zero by operating system at launch.

questions.subject: C
questions.explanation: &a has type pointer-to-array int(*)[5]. &a + 1 moves pointer past the entire array. Casting to int* and (p-1) points to a[4] = 5.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the value of expression (1U << 31) on 32-bit two's complement system?
questions.explanation: Shifting 1U into 31st position sets the sign bit, representing 0x80000000 (-2147483648 in signed 32-bit context).

questions.subject: C
questions.question: Given int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }, what is the correct syntax to invoke this function via function pointer fp?
questions.explanation: In C, calling function pointer can use either explicit dereference (*fp)(a, b) or implicit syntax fp(a, b).

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What does the expression 2[arr] evaluate to where arr is an array of integers?

options.B: arr[2] because a[b] is *(a + b) and addition is commutative

questions.explanation: In C, arr[2] is defined as *(arr + 2). Due to commutative property of addition, *(2 + arr) is 2[arr].

questions.subject: C
questions.topic: Undefined behavior and common programming errors
questions.question: What happens if you dereference a pointer converted from an unaligned memory address on strict alignment architectures?

options.B: Bus Error / Alignment Fault leading to crash

questions.explanation: Accessing misaligned addresses on hardware requiring strict alignment triggers a bus error or hardware fault exception.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: Where are local auto variables allocated during function calls?
questions.explanation: Local variables with automatic storage duration are allocated on the active execution call stack frame.

questions.subject: C
questions.explanation: #x stringifies 'val' to "val". String literal concatenation joins "val" and " = %d\n" into "val = %d\n", printing 'val = 10'.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What does char (*a[10])(int) declare?

options.A: A function returning array of 10 char pointers
options.B: An array of 10 function pointers, each pointing to a function taking int and returning char

questions.explanation: a[10] is an array of 10 pointers (*) to functions taking (int) parameter and returning char.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What attribute or pragma is used in GCC/Clang to disable structure padding?
questions.explanation: __attribute__((packed)) forces the compiler to minimize space without inserting padding alignment bytes.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: Which function in C11 aligned dynamic memory allocation allocates 'size' bytes whose address is a multiple of 'alignment'?
questions.explanation: C11 standard introduced aligned_alloc(alignment, size) in <stdlib.h> for aligned dynamic memory allocation.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the time complexity of solving the Tower of Hanoi problem for N disks?
questions.explanation: Tower of Hanoi recurrence T(N) = 2T(N-1) + 1 yields exponential time complexity O(2^N).

questions.subject: C
questions.question: How do you swap two integer variables x and y without using a temporary variable via bitwise operations?

options.A: x = x ^ y; y = x ^ y; x = x ^ y;
options.B: x = x & y; y = x & y; x = x & y;
options.C: x = x | y; y = x | y; x = x | y;

questions.explanation: The XOR swap algorithm uses three XOR operations to exchange values without extra memory.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: In C, what is the sequence point guarantee of logical AND (&&) operator?

options.B: Left operand is fully evaluated and side effects applied before right operand is evaluated (short-circuiting)

questions.explanation: The && operator introduces a sequence point after evaluating left operand, guaranteeing left-to-right evaluation and short-circuiting.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is a Stack Overflow error caused by in C program execution?

options.A: Allocating too much memory via malloc
options.B: Exceeding available stack memory limits, usually due to infinite recursion or huge stack arrays

questions.explanation: Stack overflow occurs when call stack memory limit is exceeded by excessive stack allocation or deep recursion.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: In a circular queue implemented using array of size N, what is the formula for next index after 'rear'?
questions.explanation: Modulo arithmetic (rear + 1) % N wraps index back to 0 when reaching array end.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What happens when a negative signed integer is converted to an unsigned integer type of same width in C?

options.B: Value is converted by adding 2^N (where N is bit width), resulting in large positive integer

questions.explanation: Converting negative signed to unsigned performs modular reduction modulo 2^N in accordance with C standard binary representation.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the average time complexity of Heap Sort?
questions.explanation: Heap sort maintains heap structure and performs N extractions taking O(N log N) time in all cases.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: Which standard library function uses function pointers for custom sorting comparison callback?
questions.explanation: Both qsort() and bsearch() accept comparator function pointers int (*compar)(const void*, const void*).

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the purpose of fflush(stdout) in C?

options.B: Forces immediate flushing of stdout output stream buffer to terminal/destination

questions.explanation: fflush(stdout) forces buffered pending output bytes to be written immediately to output file/device.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is guaranteed about argv[argc] in standard C main signature?

options.B: It is strictly a NULL pointer

questions.explanation: The C standard mandates that argv[argc] must be a NULL pointer.

questions.subject: C
questions.topic: Strict aliasing and effective type fundamentals
questions.question: Which pointer type is explicitly permitted by C standard to alias any object type without violating strict aliasing?
questions.explanation: Character types (char*, unsigned char*) are special target types allowed to inspect/alias raw bytes of any object.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: Which header file provides macros va_start, va_arg, and va_end for handling variadic functions in C?
questions.explanation: <stdarg.h> defines macros to step through variable argument lists in C variadic functions.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the result of subtracting two pointers pointing to elements of the same array in C (p2 - p1)?

options.B: Difference in number of array elements between them (ptrdiff_t)

questions.explanation: Pointer subtraction returns the element index difference between pointers as signed integer type ptrdiff_t.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is thread_local (or _Thread_local in C11) storage class specifier used for?

options.A: Making variable global across all threads
options.B: Giving variable thread storage duration where each thread has its own distinct instance

questions.explanation: _Thread_local creates thread-specific storage instances isolated per execution thread.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is a flexible array member in a C structure (C99 feature)?

options.B: An array of unsized length char arr[] as last member of struct used for dynamic allocation payloads

questions.explanation: Flexible array members allow a structure's last member to have incomplete array type [] for variable-sized heap allocations.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the result of accessing uninitialized local variable with automatic storage duration in C?
questions.explanation: Reading uninitialized automatic variables yields indeterminate values, causing undefined behavior.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: How do you clear (set to 0) the k-th bit of an integer n (0-indexed)?
questions.explanation: Bitwise AND with bitwise NOT mask ~(1 << k) clears the k-th bit while preserving all other bits.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'const' qualifier on a variable declaration?

options.B: Informs compiler that variable value cannot be modified after initialization

questions.explanation: 'const' specifies read-only immutability for the qualified object.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the average time complexity of searching in a balanced Binary Search Tree (BST)?
questions.explanation: A balanced BST halves search space at each tree level, yielding logarithmic O(log N) search time.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is a major advantage of a Doubly Linked List over a Singly Linked List?

options.B: Allows bidirectional traversal (forward and backward) and O(1) deletion of given node pointer

questions.explanation: Doubly linked lists store previous node pointers, enabling reverse traversal and constant-time node removal.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: Which standard header file provides signal handling functions like signal() and raise() in C?
questions.explanation: <signal.h> contains facility definitions for handling asynchronous signal conditions in C.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What does the 'volatile' keyword inform the C compiler?

options.A: Variable should be stored in GPU memory
options.B: Variable value may be modified by hardware or external threads, preventing compiler caching in registers

questions.explanation: 'volatile' prevents compiler optimizations that cache values in registers or reorder accesses to memory.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is printed by printf("%d", sizeof('a')) in standard C (unlike C++)?
questions.explanation: In C, character constants like 'a' have type 'int' (sizeof('a') == sizeof(int)), whereas in C++ they have type 'char'.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What is the result of expression (n & -n) for integer n?

options.A: Isolates the lowest set bit of n

questions.explanation: In two's complement, (n & -n) isolates and extracts the rightmost lowest 1-bit of n.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What does the static analysis tool 'cppcheck' do for C applications?

options.B: Inspects source code without execution to identify bugs, memory leaks, and undefined behavior

questions.explanation: Cppcheck is a static code analysis tool that analyzes C/C++ source code for potential bugs and security vulnerabilities without running the binary.

questions.subject: C
questions.question: What feature was introduced in C11 standard for type-generic macro expressions?
questions.explanation: C11 introduced the _Generic keyword, enabling selection of expressions based on argument type at compile time.
